messages.author: 65bd0f277ec81ba2
messages.subject: BYM2, overfitting and PC priors
parts:
Hi,

I fitted a BYM2 with priors

list(phi = list(prior = "pc", param = c(.5, .7)),
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, .01)))

This model has a correlation of 0.999987 between observed and fitted values. The hyperparameters are:

                          mean   sd
Precision for id  2.67     0.48
Phi for id            0.80     0.11

I thought that overfitting could be reduced with a higher penalty that increases the precision and decreases Phi. The following priors increases the precision and reduces Phi but do not reduce overfitting.

list(phi = list(prior = "pc", param = c(.3, .9)),
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(.01, .01)))

This second model has a correlation of 0.9999575 between observed and fitted values. The hyperparameters are:
mean sd
Precision for id  9.02     0.74
Phi for id            0.36     0.09

Why overfitting do not decrease?

Thanks in advance

What I wonder is that although priors in m2 impose a stronger penalty that change the hyperparameters, the model still predict training data almost perfectly. Should not the priors in m2 reduce model complexity (as reflected in the hyperparameters) and consequently reduce prediction accuracy in training data?

The situation does not change even if I use the following prior:

prior2 <-list(phi = list(prior = "pc", param = c(.01, .09)),
                   prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(.001, .001)))

I am using INLA_17.12.01

Oswaldo
